analysis:
This batch contains only documentation changes: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/deadline-admission-estimators.md, lines 1-6) and a new hardware-support.md section titled 'Deadline admission rates' (head 457-482), plus a code-map row at head line 536. Together they describe changes to the first-token deadline admission estimators: decode is charged per batch step, with MTP depth capped by the verification envelope; the isolated-prefill rate is floored at 1/8 of the calibration anchor; idle evidence older than 30 minutes is treated as absent; measurement age is tied to the newest observation; and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 acts as a rollback, forwarded by darkbloom start to the launchd-managed provider. The docs state that these estimators are a time check only. They say no KV grant, load quotation, activation floor, serving width or memory concurrency changes, and that slot and process byte admission still applies. They also say the published rates and capacity wire fields are unchanged.

Against the threat model, the closest concern is T-041/SEC-035 (TTFT timing oracle). The estimators shape admission, not prefix-cache reuse or cache scoping, so the accepted same-account oracle is not widened on the evidence shown. There is also a DoS angle (ADV-002): admission could become more permissive, admitting more deadline work. The docs claim memory admission is preserved, but the Swift implementation is not supplied.

Integration should verify the following in source:
- AdmissionRateEstimators.swift and EngineV2Bridge+Admission.swift (targetFirstTokenDeadlineAdmission) do not bypass slot or ProcessMemoryLedger admission.
- The anchorFloorFraction floor cannot let an operator-manipulated calibration inflate rates in published capacity fields.
- Env forwarding in darkbloom start is limited to this variable and does not leak other environment variables into the launchd plist.

No security regression is evidenced in these docs-only units.
